correctness.rationale: Support and four linear comparison signs classify every original-language sentence. Explicit integer rescaling to absolute coordinate sum at most 3, followed by support-preserving reconstruction, proves every complete type has a model of size ≤7. The support-count \(4+18+28+17=67\) is exhaustive. Jiang Theorem 3.16 restricts spectra to integer or even tails; exact witnesses realize all 11 and one needs ≥7. checker.py evaluates all 64 original sentence forms directly through size 10, confirms the reduction on 46,375 tuples through size 30, and tests witness spectra through 28. No finite computation is used as proof of an infinite statement.

value.rationale: After the unrestricted-spectrum classification, fixed noun-vocabulary expressive thresholds are a substantive natural question. The sharp jump from one-noun cutoff 3 to two-noun cutoff 7, exact eleven spectra, and complete 67 sign-support profiles identify what cardinality constraints can be seen in the first nontrivial joint-predicate fragment. Seven-point reduction is a uniform small-model decision procedure, not an arbitrary finite table.
